authority: Shawn's word, distilled in ~/workspace/team-nitro/THE-NAYA-DESIGN-LAWS.md (the human language). This file is the same law, in machine form. Where they disagree, the human book wins and this file is fixed the same pass.
never_sample_from_screenshots: The reference photographs show BRIGHT values (vortex 8 ≈ #f050f0 vs locked #6d28d9; tier $ gold ≈ #f0b030 vs locked #d4a017). Hues and order in the pictures are right; values are not. Take hexes from tokens.deep_palette, never from a screenshot.

checks.checker: check-design-laws.py — run it on the built file before shipping. Exit 1 means a law is broken; fix it, don't argue with it.
eye_only: flat-or-dead (hover every object; a board that does nothing on hover is unfinished)
flow (never the same color twice in a row — check by eye down every row)
harvested-verbatim (name the reference object each element was measured against)
read-as-a-reader (top to bottom — Shawn's eye is the final gate)

machine_checkable.rule: No gray color value anywhere (any hex gray, 'gray'/'grey', dim tokens).
No font-size below 17px in text rules.

machine_checkable.method: regex over color: declarations; var(--*) references pass (variables resolve to the scale)
machine_checkable.rule: Every literal color: value is in text_colors_allowed.
File contains :hover rules (objects must answer touch).

name: THE-NAYA-DESIGN-LAWS — machine language

black.note: Inside of every icon, button, board. Harvested verbatim from the Smart Note board. Never off-black.

motion.note: Slow is premium. Fast motion feels cheap.

tokens.text_colors_forbidden_note: Gray at any size, any value. Red/orange/magenta/pink as TEXT (they stay legal as rim/orb/board colors — the rule is for words, §2.2 of the human book).

type_scale_px.note: Official, all the way through. No text smaller than 17. Digit tiles and display numerals keep their harvested scale — they are numbers, not text.
